data.title: What’s Ahead for the Stock Market This Week
data.description:
After Friday’s sharp selloff triggered by President Trump’s decision to raise tariffs in response to China tightening rare earth exports, investors are starting the week on edge. The focus now shifts to trade tensions, earnings season, and the Federal Reserve’s next moves.

Big Earnings Week: Banks and Chipmakers Take Center Stage

This week kicks off a busy stretch of third-quarter results from major financial firms and tech companies.

  • Banks: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Citigroup all report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Later in the week, American Express, Truist Financial, and State Street will wrap up the financial lineup.
  • Tech & Chips: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) reports Thursday after strong AI chip sales boosted its revenue 40% in the first half of 2025. ASML follows on Wednesday after raising concerns about tariffs and slowing demand for chip equipment.
  • Tech events: Oracle’s AI World conference begins Monday, and Salesforce’s Dreamforce starts Tuesday — both likely to bring attention to artificial intelligence and enterprise tech. Earnings Calendar >>

Data Delays and Fed Watch

The federal government shutdown, now entering its third week, is likely to delay several key reports, including retail sales, inflation (PPI), housing starts, and jobless claims. Some data will still come through, like the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index on Tuesday and homebuilder confidence on Thursday.

Investors will also tune in to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech on Tuesday, along with comments from Fed officials, including Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller. The Fed’s Beige Book, which gives an overview of economic conditions across regions, will be released on Wednesday.

Market Context

Bond markets will be closed on Monday for Columbus Day (also observed as Indigenous Peoples Day), but stock exchanges will remain open.

With limited economic data and uncertainty around Washington’s budget standoff, markets are likely to take their cues from corporate earnings and Fed commentary.

In short, this week is about navigating through noise — balancing worries over tariffs and the shutdown against potential optimism from strong bank and chipmaker earnings.

data.title: What Is the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA)? A Complete Guide
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), often referred to as the Dow Jones, the Dow 30, or simply the Dow, is one of the world’s most recognized stock market indexes. The DJIA tracks 30 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States, making it a widely followed indicator of the overall health of the U.S. economy and stock market. Investors searching for DJIA today, DJIA futures, or Dow Jones price updates often turn to this index as a barometer of market sentiment.

But what exactly is the DJIA, what stocks does it include, and how do traders and long-term investors use it in their strategies?

What Is the DJIA?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a price-weighted index created in 1896 by Charles Dow and Edward Jones. Unlike market-cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, the DJIA assigns weight based on a stock’s price rather than its market capitalization. This means a company with a higher stock price (e.g., Apple or UnitedHealth) influences the index more heavily than lower-priced stocks.

The DJIA is designed to reflect the performance of blue-chip companies across different sectors of the U.S. economy. It does not include utilities or transportation stocks, which are tracked by separate Dow indexes.

What Companies Are in the DJIA?

The DJIA is composed of 30 large, publicly traded U.S. companies that are considered leaders in their industries. These companies span sectors such as technology, finance, healthcare, consumer goods, and industrials.

Here’s a snapshot of the DJIA holdings (as of 2025, September 15th):

Note: The index is reviewed periodically, and constituents may change depending on mergers, bankruptcies, or shifts in market relevance.

How Does the DJIA Work?

  • Price-Weighted Methodology: Higher-priced stocks have more influence.
  • Dow Divisor: A proprietary number adjusted for stock splits, dividends, and corporate actions ensures continuity.
  • Sector Balance: While tech stocks (Apple, Microsoft) now hold significant weight, the index aims to represent the broader U.S. economy.

If Apple (AAPL) rises $5 in a day, it has the same impact on the DJIA as Boeing (BA) rising $5, even though their market caps differ drastically.

Why Do Investors Watch the DJIA?

  • Economic Barometer: The DJIA today is seen as a snapshot of the U.S. economy.
  • Historical Importance: Created in 1896, it has over 125 years of market history.
  • Market Sentiment: Widely quoted on news outlets and financial platforms.
  • Trading Opportunities: Investors follow DJIA futures, DJIA ETFs, and Dow Jones index funds for exposure.

How to Trade or Invest in the DJIA

Investors can’t buy the DJIA directly but can gain exposure through exchange-traded funds (ETFs), futures contracts, or mutual funds:

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) – tracks the DJIA closely.
  • DJIA Futures – contracts traded on CME, allowing leveraged exposure.
  • Index Funds – designed for long-term buy-and-hold investors.

data.title: Ross Stores Sales Rise 12% and Holiday Comparable-Sales Outlook Holds
data.description:
Ross Stores (NASDAQ: ROST) reported a 12% rise in quarterly sales to $6.3 billion on November 19. More shoppers visited its stores, lifting comparable sales 8%. The retailer raised its full-year earnings outlook and kept its forecast for holiday-quarter comparable-sales growth at 4% to 5%.

For the quarter ended October 31, net income rose to $606 million from $512 million a year earlier, according to Ross’s earnings release. Diluted earnings increased to $1.91 a share from $1.58. Operating margin rose 0.7 percentage point to 12.3%.

The 8% comparable-sales gain topped the 6% to 7% range Ross gave in August. The unchanged holiday forecast implies a slower pace of growth, Reuters reported. The holiday quarter also faces a tougher comparison after comparable sales rose 9% in the same period last year. Ross expects fourth-quarter earnings of $2.16 to $2.25 a share.

The retailer now projects fiscal 2026 earnings of $8.75 to $8.84 a share, up from $8.61 to $8.77. The new range still includes about 60 cents a share from a tariff refund recognized in the second quarter.

data.title: Japan’s Core Inflation Rises to 2.2% Ahead of December Rate Decision
data.description:
Japan’s core consumer prices rose 2.2% from a year earlier in October, up from 2.1% in September. The Statistics Bureau’s November 20 release put headline inflation at 2.3%. Japan’s core measure excludes fresh food and includes energy.

The core figure came in below the 2.3% median forecast in a Reuters poll. The index excluding both fresh food and energy also rose 2.2% year over year, slowing from 2.4% in September. Goods prices rose 3.2%, compared with 1.4% for services, Reuters reported.

The Bank of Japan held its short-term policy rate around 1.25% in October in an 8–1 vote. One member preferred 1.5%. A majority of analysts polled by Reuters expect a rate increase in December, when the bank meets December 17–18.

The inflation release follows the first estimate showing a marginal contraction in third-quarter output. Core inflation has now exceeded the bank’s 2% target for two months, while the measure stripping out energy and fresh food has cooled. Both figures will inform the December decision.

data.title: Intuit Agrees to Sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 Billion
data.description:
Intuit (NASDAQ: INTU) agreed on November 19 to sell its Mailchimp email-marketing business to Bending Spoons (NASDAQ: BSP) at a $3.68 billion enterprise value. The proposed sale comes five years after Intuit bought the business for about $12 billion.

Intuit expects about $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in Bending Spoons stock. In its SEC filing, Bending Spoons described an all-cash acquisition paired with a $368 million investment by Intuit in newly issued buyer shares. The companies expect the deal to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary conditions.

Intuit said in its quarterly release that it intends to use the cash proceeds for share repurchases during fiscal 2027 once the deal closes. Its 2021 quarterly filing puts the original purchase consideration at $12 billion, including $5.7 billion in cash and about $6.3 billion in Intuit stock.

Mailchimp’s revenue fell 1% to $313 million in the quarter ended October 31, while Intuit’s total revenue rose 12% to $4.4 billion. Intuit lowered its full-year sales growth forecast to 8%–9% from 9%–10%, Reuters reported. Intuit attributed the revision to Credit Karma and kept its annual earnings guidance in place. The outlook excludes the pending sale.

data.title: U.S. Jobless Claims Edge Up to 203,000 as Mid-Atlantic Factory Growth Slows
data.description:
New U.S. unemployment claims rose by 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 in the week ended November 14, the Labor Department said on November 19. A separate Philadelphia Fed survey showed factory growth slowed in the Mid-Atlantic in November, while more manufacturers reported higher prices.

The Labor Department revised the previous week’s initial claims up to 202,000 from 200,000. The four-week average rose by 2,000 to 197,750. The latest weekly total exceeded the 197,000 forecast in a Reuters poll.

Continuing claims, which track people receiving benefits after an initial week, increased by 70,000 to 1.763 million in the week ended November 7. Reuters reported that the total reached its highest level since late August and that Michigan accounted for much of the unadjusted increase.

The Philadelphia Fed’s survey showed its general activity index falling to 6.3 from 20.9, its lowest reading in six months. A positive reading means more manufacturers reported expansion than contraction. The new orders index slipped to −0.4, while the prices paid and prices received indexes rose to 58.2 and 47.0, respectively.

The claims figures measure national unemployment-benefit filings. The factory survey covers a single Federal Reserve district. Its employment index rose even as fewer firms reported overall growth.

data.title: PDD Beats Profit Estimates as Transaction Revenue Falls 12%
data.description:
PDD Holdings (NASDAQ: PDD), the parent of Temu and Pinduoduo, reported adjusted profit above Wall Street estimates on November 19. Sales were virtually flat as lower transaction-services revenue offset growth in online marketing.

Quarterly revenue was RMB108.3 billion, below the RMB115.97 billion average estimate compiled by LSEG, Reuters reported. Adjusted net income attributable to shareholders was RMB31 billion, above the RMB28.03 billion estimate and down from RMB31.4 billion a year earlier.

The earnings release showed a 12% increase in online marketing services and other revenue to RMB59.8 billion. Transaction-services revenue fell 12% to RMB48.5 billion. Sales and marketing expenses fell by RMB5 billion to RMB25.3 billion, accounting for most of the reduction in operating expenses. Reported net profit attributable to shareholders edged up to RMB29.5 billion from RMB29.3 billion.

The results cover the three months ended September 30. They provide a separate view of the group’s finances following this week’s preliminary EU findings on Temu. The financial release reports revenue by service category and gives no separate figures for Temu.

data.title: Alibaba AI Cloud Revenue Climbs 53%, but Cash Outflow Widens
data.description:
Alibaba (NYSE: BABA) reported a 53% jump in AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue on November 19. The business brought in RMB61 billion in the September quarter, while spending on cloud infrastructure helped push the group’s free cash outflow higher.

Group revenue rose 10% from a year earlier to RMB271.5 billion. Revenue from external cloud customers grew 64%, and the cloud segment’s adjusted earnings before interest, taxes and amortization more than doubled to RMB8.8 billion, according to the quarterly release.

Reuters reported that total revenue exceeded estimates. Adjusted diluted earnings of RMB8.10 per American depositary share rose 86% year over year but fell short of the RMB11.16 analysts expected. Reported net income more than tripled to RMB64.4 billion, helped by investment gains and higher operating income.

Free cash flow was negative RMB34.5 billion, compared with negative RMB21.8 billion a year earlier. Alibaba attributed the change mainly to higher cloud infrastructure spending. Smaller losses at Taobao Instant Commerce and greater customer prepayments for cloud services partly offset that spending.

data.title: Nasdaq Futures Lead Rebound Ahead of Anthropic Debut; Walmart and Claims Await
data.description:
U.S. stock futures rose before the open on Thursday, November 19, 2026, led by the Nasdaq, as Anthropic prepared for its record IPO debut. The rebound follows the S&P 500’s fifth straight loss, a sharp health-insurer selloff and Federal Reserve minutes pointing toward further rate increases. Walmart’s earnings and fresh labor-market data provide today’s next tests.

At 4:50 a.m. ET Thursday, delayed CNBC futures quotes showed December Nasdaq-100 contracts up 1.96%, S&P 500 futures up 1.10% and Dow futures up 0.61%. These are overnight futures moves, ahead of the regular cash session. In today’s pre-market video briefing, we examine the same contrast between renewed technology buying and pressure from insurance stocks and interest rates.

At Wednesday’s November 18 regular-session close, the S&P 500 was at 7,323.63, down 16.90 points, or 0.2%; the Dow lost 561.25 points, or 1.1%, to 50,198.17; and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.4% to 24,429.88. The S&P’s losing streak was its longest since June, according to the Associated Press. Unlike the setup in yesterday’s briefing, Anthropic’s pricing and the Fed minutes are now known.

Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 each, above its earlier $70–$78 range. The $81.3 billion offering, including shares sold by existing holders, exceeds SpaceX’s $75 billion June IPO, Renaissance Capital reported. Trading is expected to begin today on Nasdaq under ANT. The offer price is distinct from the first public trading price.

Health insurers remain a separate source of pressure. UnitedHealth (NYSE: UNH) closed Wednesday at $349.91, down 10.21%, while Humana (NYSE: HUM) fell 12.98% to $385.78, according to Yahoo Finance price data. The losses extended Tuesday’s decline after CMS proposed tougher Medicare Advantage audits. MLQ.ai’s report describes extrapolating sample audit findings to estimate broader overpayments. This remains a proposal; CMS says comments close January 19, 2027.

The October 27–28 Fed minutes, released Wednesday, showed almost all participants considered further rate increases likely appropriate under their baseline outlooks. A couple said an increase exceeding 25 basis points could merit consideration at the next meeting if inflation data were unfavorable. Many also saw the AI buildout as a material inflation risk. The next meeting is December 8–9; the minutes do not commit the Fed to a particular move.

Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW) rose 8.84% to $369.97 in premarket trading at 5:00 a.m. ET Thursday, according to CNBC. Its fiscal first-quarter release showed revenue up 39% to $3.44 billion and adjusted diluted earnings of $1.05 a share. It raised its annual outlook, forecasting fiscal 2027 revenue of $14.52 billion–$14.57 billion, and announced a proposed $4.5 billion all-stock acquisition of Applied Compute, subject to closing conditions.

Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) is scheduled to release results at 7 a.m. ET, following Target’s upgraded annual outlook. Weekly jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey are due at 8:30 a.m. ET, with Hammack, Goolsbee and Barr also on Thursday’s speaking calendar. Those releases will add evidence on consumer demand and economic activity before the cash market opens.

data.title: Tencent Cloud Sales Rise 35% as Adjusted Operating Profit Falls
data.description:
Tencent (HKEX: 0700) said on November 18 that cloud services revenue grew 35% from a year earlier in the third quarter. Demand for AI services helped drive that growth, while the cost of expanding computing capacity strained cash flow and adjusted operating profit fell.

Total revenue reached RMB207.3 billion in the three months ended September 30, up 8% from a year earlier and below the RMB210.77 billion LSEG estimate, Reuters reported. Revenue growth slowed from 11% in the second quarter. Domestic game revenue grew 11%, while international game revenue fell 9% against a stronger year-earlier comparison.

Adjusted operating profit fell 6% to RMB68.1 billion, and the corresponding margin fell to 33% from 38%, according to Tencent’s earnings release. On an IFRS basis, operating profit fell 7% to RMB59.1 billion. Profit attributable to shareholders rose 0.8% to RMB63.6 billion, according to the exchange filing.

Capital expenditure payments more than tripled to RMB65.1 billion from a year earlier. The company reported negative free cash flow of RMB69.1 billion and said the figure would have been positive RMB16.9 billion excluding prepayments for computing capacity. Tencent said those advance payments support both its own AI products and demand from cloud customers.
